The viewer now serves a permalink IN PLACE: GET /<todoid>/<path...> returns 200 with the whole todo rendered and focused on the object the path resolves to, replacing the 302-to-fragment from todo:71fabcb7. Verified end-to-end against the live store: /11038f9a/workitem/3 and /11038f9a/objid/000e both render 200 with zero redirects and identical focus, /summary/raw focuses the Summary section, a bogus path 404s. Body.raw:
Correction to the unlanded permalink work in todo:71fabcb7 (branch
71fabcb7-objid-stable-object-ids, 8 commits, not yet merged). That branch
resolves a permalink server-side and then 302-redirects to
/?id=<Id>#obj-<objid>. The redirect is wrong.

## The requirement

Handed http://localhost:8765/d56d/workitem/1 I expect the MAIN WEB VIEW of
todo d56d, scrolled to and focused on that item -- not a redirect elsewhere.
The URL may carry the rich js-like path; the SERVER resolves it and renders
"whole d56d" + "focus on objid:23".

This makes the path honest. The resource genuinely is "todo d56d, focused at
objid 23" -- a legitimate view of a primary resource, served 200. The earlier
design had the URL promise a sub-resource and the server answer "go look at
the parent document"; that mismatch is what this removes. Server-side
resolution is retained, so todo_url, objid stamping and nearest_objid all
survive unchanged -- only the HTTP response layer moves.

## ALL client-side UI nav is keyed by objid

Today the page uses three different key spaces:
  - work items: data-idx (a POSITION), with DATA.workitems an array indexed
    by that position
  - subtodos: data-st = the child TODO ID
  - parents: data-parent = the parent TODO ID
All three collapse to one: data-obj = objid, over a single DATA.objects map.
Position-keyed client state is the same fragility as position-keyed URLs --
that is why "ALL".

## Ratified decisions

- Clicking a box rewrites the address bar to /<todoid>/objid/<objid> with
  history.replaceState -- always a copyable permalink to what is on screen,
  and Back still means "the page before this todo" rather than unwinding
  every selection.
- /<todoid> becomes the canonical page URL; subtodo/parent box links and
  search-result links emit it. ?id= keeps working so links already pasted
  into todo bodies, commits and chat do not break. No flag day.
- A permalink to something that is not a clickable box (Summary, Scope, a Tag
  element) scrolls to and marks that SECTION: the Summary/Body/Fields sections
  get objid anchors too, so every stamped object is reachable. That is what
  makes the grammar worth having.
- Focus means exactly what a click means today: .active on the box, its commit
  message + diff in the fold, plus scrollIntoView (the work-items row scrolls
  horizontally, so a later item is off-screen without it).

## Removed from the 71fabcb7 branch

- todo_web._permalink()s 302 and permalink_target()
- the #obj-<objid> fragment and the :target CSS rule
Both are superseded by rendering the focused view at the path.

Summary.raw: permalink renders the focused todo view; unify all client nav on objid

WorkItems.message:
refactor(todo): key all client-side viewer nav on objid

The page used three key spaces: data-idx (a POSITION) for work items over a
position-indexed DATA.workitems array, and the child TODO ID for both
data-st and data-parent over two id-keyed maps. All three collapse to one
data-obj=<objid> attribute over a single DATA.objects map. Position-keyed
client state is the same fragility as position-keyed URLs, which is the whole
reason objids exist.

Cross-highlighting is resolved to objids SERVER-side: each entry carries a
'hi' list of the objids to mark when it is selected (a work item names the
subtodo row it references, a subtodo names the work items referencing it).
No browser code matches on a child todo id or a list index any more; the three
click handlers become one select(objid).

_anchor becomes _box_attrs, emitting id= (scroll target) and data-obj
(selection key) together. Behavior is unchanged -- this is the re-key only;
serving the focused view at the path comes next.

Tests: PermalinkAnchorTests.test_client_model_is_objid_only asserts the stale
keys are GONE (not merely unused) and that DATA is {id, objects} with hex
keys; the existing subtodo-reference test now asserts the cross-link in objid
terms and that the child todo id does not appear in the work item's entry at
all. Full suite green (446); pylint 10.00/10.
WorkItems.summary: [MIDCAP] Re-key the client model to objid: data-obj on work-item/subtodo/parent boxes, a single DATA.objects map keyed by objid replacing the idx-indexed DATA.workitems array and the two todo-id-keyed maps, click handlers looking up by objid. Behavior identical; no client code reads a list index. Tests assert no data-idx remains and selection still works.

WorkItems.message:
feat(todo): make non-box sections permalink targets

A permalink can resolve to an object that has no clickable box -- Summary,
Body, Scope, a Tag element. Those now carry addressing attributes so the link
has something to scroll to and mark.

Sections are ADDRESSABLE but not SELECTABLE, which is why this is data-objs
rather than data-obj: there is nothing to open in the fold. It is a
space-separated list (CSS ~= matches it) because one row can display several
stamped objects -- the Tag field renders every element together and a DOM id
can only name one of them.

_objids_within walks a field value for the objids it contains; _section_attrs
emits id= for the first plus data-objs for all. Gated on interactive, same as
boxes, so a static rendition in the fold never emits another id scope's ids.
_meta_html wraps each field in a .meta-row div to hang the attributes on and
now takes the interactive flag.

Tests: PermalinkAnchorTests.test_non_box_sections_are_addressable -- Summary,
Body and Scope carry their objid as an id, and the Tag row lists both element
objids in data-objs.
WorkItems.summary: [MIDCAP] Section anchors: carry each stamped section's objid (Summary, Body, Fields rows) into the rendered HTML so a non-box permalink target is reachable and markable.

WorkItems.message:
feat(todo): render_todo_page opens focused on a permalink's object

render_todo_page(root, todo, focus_objid=...) embeds the resolved objid as
FOCUS, and the page opens with that object already selected: for a box, the
exact state a click produces (.active, its message and diff in the fold); for
an addressable section, a .focus marker. Either way scrollIntoView, because
the work-items row scrolls horizontally and a later item is off-screen until
we scroll it -- 'SCROLLED to the item' is the requirement, not just 'the right
page'.

An objid that is not on the page is ignored and the todo renders normally, so
a stale or cross-scope link degrades to 'the right todo' rather than an error.

The fragment-era ':target' CSS becomes an explicit .focus class, which also
covers sections (marked, not selected -- they have nothing to put in the fold).

Tests: RenderFocusTest in test_todo_web_permalink.py -- the focus objid is
embedded and its box exists, a section objid is embedded and its data-objs
target exists, and the default render is unfocused. The focusing itself is
browser JS, so what is pinned here is the server's half of the contract; the
test docstring says so rather than implying the JS ran.
WorkItems.summary: [MIDCAP] Server-side focus: render_todo_page(root, todo, focus_objid=...) sets the initial selection -- .active on the box, its message+diff in the fold, scrollIntoView on load; a section target scrolls and marks the section. Tests via --dump-html.

WorkItems.message:
feat(todo): serve the focused todo view at the permalink path

Replaces the 302. GET /<todoid>/<path...> now returns 200 with the whole todo
rendered and focused on the object the path resolves to. The path IS the
resource -- 'todo d56d, focused on objid 23' -- so a permalink that bounced
you to a different URL was never the durable name it claimed to be, and left
the address bar disagreeing with the link you were handed.

Deleted: permalink_target, the #obj-<objid> redirect target, todo_url's
nearest_objid, and the now-unused quote import.

Added resolve_focus(root, todo, segments) and todo_url.objid_chain, which
returns the enclosing objids innermost-first. Resolving to something the page
cannot DRAW is not an error: WorkItems.2.execution is stamped but never
rendered on its own, so the chain is walked outward to the work item that
contains it. A path with nothing focusable above it (the State subtree) renders
the todo unfocused rather than 404 -- the link still means 'this todo'.
_focusable_objids is the set the walk stops at: every box, plus every
addressable section.

An unresolvable path is still 404, and /favicon.ico and friends keep theirs.

Tests: test_todo_web_permalink.py rewritten off Location headers onto rendered
content -- ResolveFocusTest (9 cases incl. the walk-out from an undrawn
execution block, reachable now that the fixture carries one) and
PermalinkRouteTest asserting 200 + FOCUS + the whole todo in the body, the
unfocusable path rendering anyway, both 404s, ?id= still rendering, and
/search untouched. Full suite green (454); pylint 10.00/10.

WorkItems.message:
docs(todo): permalinks render in place, focused

Rewrites the SKILL.md Permalinks section for the render-in-place model. The
viewer serves /<todoid>/<path...> as 200 -- the whole todo, scrolled to and
focused on the object the path resolves to, in the state clicking that box
produces. No redirect: the path IS the resource. /<todoid> is the canonical
page URL and every internal link emits it; ?id= still works.

Adds a table of how a link DEGRADES, which is the part worth writing down:
a scalar focuses its enclosing box, an object the viewer does not draw focuses
the nearest one it does, a section is scrolled to and marked, the State subtree
renders unfocused, and only an unresolvable path is a 404.

Also documents that clicking rewrites the address bar (replaceState) so what
is on screen is already copyable, that all client-side selection is objid-keyed,
and why resolution must be server-side (prefix matching needs the record; a
fragment never reaches the server).

The web subcommand's doc_long gains the permalink route and the address-bar
behavior.

SKILL.md's one non-ASCII character (line 554) predates this branch and is
outside the edited sections; everything authored here is 7-bit clean.
WorkItems.summary: [LOCAP] SKILL.md: rewrite the Permalinks section for the render-in-place model (no redirect, server resolves and focuses), and note that all client-side nav is objid-keyed.
